title: Correct tenant double-apportionment during cross-region fallback
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Several customers reported duplicated charges after an automatic cross-region fallback event. Investigations show certain retry/fallback paths produced two separate metering events for the same logical request across Hosted and Dedicated/private metering pipelines, resulting in double-apportioned token accounting on invoices. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, fixes, rollout, and customer remediation.
reproduction_steps: Simulate a primary-region GPU pool outage for tenant 'acme-corp' by introducing region failure in test harness
Send a burst of streaming generation requests with streaming retries enabled and client-supplied idempotency missing
Force the smart-router to fallback to a secondary region where dedicated/private routes exist
Observe metering logs: two separate meter events emitted with different route_context ids but the same user-session and start/end timestamps
Validate invoice simulation: ledger shows two line-items for overlapping token ranges for the same session
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - Initial triage: alerted by Customer Success on three enterprise customers with ~2x token usage for the fallback window
2026-03-11 - Found that fallback path did not propagate the original request's meter_dedup_key header to the downstream dedicated metering gateway
2026-03-12 - Noted dedicated/private deployments run a separate metering aggregator with eventual-consistency window of 30s; if dedup key missing both aggregators independently emitted events
2026-03-12 - Router emitted a retry with X-Route-Context new value; meters attributed by route_context resulting in two ledger attributions
2026-03-13 - Edge case: streaming requests that resumed after prefetch/KV warm-up created overlapping token ranges that our metering heuristic treated as distinct allocations
2026-03-14 - Confirmed repro in staging with a test tenant and captured full trace IDs; see trace links in 'links'
root_cause: Idempotency/dedup keys are not consistently propagated on fallback/resend across the smart-router to dedicated/private metering endpoints
Separate metering stacks (hosted vs dedicated/private) accept events without a global dedup check within the eventual-consistency window
Streaming resumption semantics (prefix replays + prefetch) created overlapping token attributions that our ledger merge step didn't compress when dedup keys differ
proposed_fix: Ensure smart-router always propagates 'X-Meter-Dedup-Key' derived from request.id (fall back to session+start_ts) when performing cross-region fallback
Introduce a short-lived global dedup index in the central metering aggregator (write-through cache with 60s TTL) to accept duplicate events from hosted/dedicated pipelines
Enhance ledger merge logic to collapse overlapping token ranges within a 5s tolerance when session and trace IDs match
Add explicit checks in dedicated/private metering ingress to reject events that lack valid dedup keys and queue them for reconciliation rather than emitting duplicates
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy router change to propagate X-Meter-Dedup-Key to canary region (runtime-1.24-canary) - 2026-03-17
2) Deploy metering-ingress validation to staging and run synthetic fallback traffic (2026-03-18)
3) Deploy central dedup cache feature flag gated; enable for 10% of customers and monitor billing dashboards (2026-03-19)
4) Gradually ramp dedup cache to 100% across hosted/dedicated/private over 48 hours if error rates and SLOs remain stable
5) Run ledger backfill and reconciliation (see backfill_plan) and issue customer credits before full rollout completes
mitigation: Short-term: temporarily disable automatic fallback to dedicated for impacted customers (CS coordinated whitelist) to prevent further duplicates
Apply targeted backfill credits for customers showing duplicated invoices while fix is deployed (billing-runbook-incident-2026-03)
Add monitoring alert rule to detect >20% token delta between generated tokens and billed tokens in any 5-minute window
backfill_plan: Export all ledger events for affected tenants between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-13
Run dedupe job using trace_id and session_id precedence to collapse duplicated events
Compute net credit per tenant and upload adjustments to billing system with a clear audit trail
Send customer-facing remediation notes and proposed credits to CS for approval before applying
tests: Unit tests for router propagation logic ensuring X-Meter-Dedup-Key present for fallback paths
Integration test simulating cross-region fallback with streaming retries covering hosted + dedicated ingress
Load test at production QPS to validate dedup cache scaling and latency impact
E2E billing simulation that verifies no duplicate ledger entries for the same logical request
